verdict: key consistent once the plaintext is read from the cipher: 71 signs = 71 letters, 59/60 repeated occurrences (98.3%); the one break is the ⊏ sign (ط in لطراز, ص in مصر). The reading fits every remark of the compiler (36r l.1-7): the superfluous vocative اي, no article, four rhyme words حلا, and حل written without alif in both lines.
notes: Text as enciphered: اي من لطراز ملك مصر حلا كم رمز مترجم اتاه حلا / تشريفك لي لمر عيشي حلا ما حل بان تذكرني ما حلا ('O you whose (robe's) embroidery is the kingship of Egypt, how sweet! How many a ciphered riddle came to him and he solved it. / Your honouring me made the bitterness of my life sweet: nothing is sweet but that you remember me, how sweet!'). Sense of the translation not checked.

Against the record: يا is اي (the compiler's 'superfluous ay ... for the vocative'); كم [?] من is كم رمز (ر م ز, with the ز sign of لطراز); the unread end بازدكرن ملحلا is بان تذكرني ما حلا (ب ا ن | ت ذ ك ر ن ي | م ا | ح ل ا). Against the record's wording: 89.3% / 91.1%.

The compiler's 'hila without alif in both lines': حل on l.12 (ما حل) has no alif sign; on l.9 the first حلا was written حل and the alif added as a small 4 above the ل sign (the record's 'small 4 written over a sign', not counted there). Read so, the four rhyme words are all حلا.

The sign in the outer right margin of l.8 (m, under a brown mark) is read as the م of من, omitted in the line (group 2 has only the ن sign). Its exact place is a judgement; it could also stand before اي.
Counts by eye: 12, 11 (with the inserted 4), 12, 11, 11, 14 = 71 (record 70). 21 dividers for the 21 word ends inside the text.
